lines.text: Why can two waves make a region quieter or darker even while both sources are operating? Their displacements add, and a stable pattern needs a stable phase relationship.

Interference is the superposition of two or more waves, producing a resultant displacement with regions of reinforcement and cancellation. Coherent waves have the same frequency and a constant phase difference. The phase difference may be non zero. Their amplitudes need not match for coherence, although equal amplitudes allow complete cancellation at destructive positions. In phase arrivals reinforce, antiphase arrivals cancel when their amplitudes are equal.
This applies to water waves, sound, light and microwaves. It builds directly on superposition, the displacement at a point is the sum of the individual wave displacements.
Interference, superposition producing maxima and minima. Coherence, same frequency and constant phase difference. Equal amplitude is needed for complete cancellation, not coherence.
Can two waves remain coherent if one source is always a quarter cycle behind the other? Explain using the definition.
A fixed pattern in a ripple tank and alternating loud and quiet positions near loudspeakers come from the same two source effect.

For water waves, connect two ripple tank dippers to the same vibrator or motor, a stroboscope or suitable camera can reveal the fixed nodal and antinodal pattern. For sound, feed two loudspeakers from one signal generator and move a microphone through the overlap region to detect alternating maxima and minima. For light, illuminate two narrow slits from one monochromatic source and observe bright and dark fringes on a screen. For microwaves, drive two sources from one oscillator and move a receiver through the overlap region. In each case the common drive provides the same frequency and constant phase difference, the waves must overlap where the pattern is observed.
The shared source implements coherence, while the detector or screen reveals where the arriving waves reinforce or cancel.

Ripple tank, two dippers, one vibrator, fixed nodal lines. Sound, two loudspeakers, one signal generator, moving microphone. Light, one monochromatic source, two slits, screen fringes. Microwaves, shared oscillator, moving receiver.
Why must the two ripple tank dippers be connected to the same motor rather than driven independently?
A pattern is useful only if its bright and dark places stay put long enough to observe.

Two source fringes are observed where waves overlap and their phase difference at each position remains constant. The sources therefore need the same frequency and a constant relative phase, coherence. For initially in phase sources, a path difference n lambda produces a maximum and open bracket n plus one half close bracket lambda a minimum. A fixed non zero initial phase difference shifts the fringe positions. Comparable amplitudes make the contrast clear, equal amplitudes allow complete cancellation at a minimum. For light, a monochromatic source helps prevent fringes of different wavelengths from washing one another out.
The apparatus in the preceding card supplies coherence, the path difference then decides whether each location is a maximum or minimum.

Overlap and coherence give a stationary pattern. In phase sources, n lambda maximum, open bracket n plus one half close bracket lambda minimum. Similar amplitudes improve contrast, equal amplitudes permit zero minima.
Why would a changing relative phase blur a fringe pattern even if both sources keep emitting?
Fringe spacing lets you determine a wavelength too small to measure directly with a ruler.

For double slit interference using light, recall and use lambda equals a x over D. Here lambda is wavelength, a is the separation of the two slits, x is the spacing between adjacent bright fringes or adjacent dark fringes, and D is the distance from the slits to the screen. Convert all measured lengths to metres before substitution. Rearranging gives x equals lambda D over a, increasing wavelength or screen distance increases spacing, increasing slit separation decreases it. Measure over several fringe intervals and divide by the number of intervals for a more reliable x.
The relation quantifies the stable light pattern produced by coherent waves from the double slit.
lambda equals a x over D for double slit light. a, slit separation, x, fringe spacing, D, slit to screen distance. Convert to metres, measure several fringe intervals.

eight point three Interference.
In one breath.
Waves that overlap add their displacements. Coherent sources maintain a fixed phase relationship, so their constructive and destructive interference forms a stable pattern.
Key ideas.

Interference is the superposition of two or more waves to produce a resultant wave with regions of reinforcement and cancellation. At a maximum, waves arrive in phase, at a minimum, they arrive in antiphase. Coherent waves have the same frequency and a constant phase difference. That phase difference need not be zero, and their amplitudes need not be equal. Equal amplitudes are needed for complete cancellation at a minimum.

For two sources initially in phase, a path difference of n lambda gives a maximum, while open bracket n plus one half close bracket lambda gives a minimum, where n is an integer. An initial phase difference shifts these positions. A visible, stationary fringe pattern needs overlapping waves of the same frequency with a constant phase difference. Similar amplitudes make its bright and dark regions easier to distinguish. For light, use a monochromatic source and a common source feeding both slits, a broad mixture of wavelengths can blur fringes.

This idealised profile shows the central part of a two slit pattern for sources emitting in phase, neglecting the variation of the diffraction envelope. Peaks mark bright fringes, the marked interval x joins adjacent bright peaks. Equal amplitudes of the two arriving waves allow zero intensity minima where they arrive in antiphase.
Method.
Water, Attach two dippers in a ripple tank to one vibrator or motor. Illuminate the surface and use a stroboscope or suitable camera to reveal fixed nodal and antinodal lines.
Sound, Connect two loudspeakers to one signal generator. Move a microphone, preferably linked to an oscilloscope, across the overlap region. Alternating high and low amplitudes reveal interference.
Light, Illuminate two narrow slits from the same monochromatic source. Their diffracted light overlaps on a distant screen, giving alternating bright and dark fringes.

Microwaves, Drive two sources from the same oscillator and move a receiver through the overlap region. It detects alternating maxima and minima. In every setup, a shared drive maintains the relative phase.

For double slit light, measure the slit separation a, screen distance D, and spacing x between adjacent bright fringes, or adjacent dark fringes. Then use lambda equals a x over D, with all lengths in metres. To reduce uncertainty, measure across several intervals and divide by the number of intervals. Since x equals lambda D over a, increasing D or wavelength widens fringes, while increasing a narrows them.
Worked example.

Slits zero point two zero millimetres apart produce fringes six point zero millimetres apart on a screen two point zero metres away. Calculate the wavelength. Use lambda equals a x over D. Convert a equals zero point two zero times ten to the minus three metres and x equals six point zero times ten to the minus three metres. lambda equals open bracket zero point two zero times ten to the minus three close bracket open bracket six point zero times ten to the minus three close bracket, all over two point zero equals six point zero times ten to the minus seven metres. The answer is six hundred nanometres.
Traps.
Trap, Coherent means exactly in phase. Why it's wrong, Coherence permits any constant phase difference. Instead, State both equal frequency and constant phase difference.
Trap, Two separately driven dippers automatically give a steady pattern. Why it's wrong, Their relative phase can drift. Instead, Drive both from one motor.
Trap, Doubling slit separation doubles fringe spacing. Why it's wrong, x is inversely proportional to a. Instead, Halve x when a doubles.
Trap, Substitute millimetres beside metres. Why it's wrong, Mixed units create powers of ten errors. Instead, Convert every length to metres first.
Exam technique.

For describe questions, name the shared source, the two emitters, the detector or screen, and the observed alternating maxima and minima. For explain, link the shared drive to a constant phase difference and fixed pattern. For calculate, write lambda equals a x over D, show S I conversion, substitute, and give a sensible number of significant figures. If a question asks for a dark fringe, check its path difference rather than using the fringe spacing formula alone.
Counting dark fringes.

For sources emitting in phase, start at the central maximum, the first dark fringe has path difference lambda over two, and the second has three lambda over two. For example, if lambda equals six hundred nanometres, these are three hundred nanometres and nine hundred nanometres. The fringe spacing x is the distance along the screen between adjacent fringes of the same kind, bright to bright or dark to dark, it is not itself a path difference between the two light paths.
